execSummary: Way2Wealth published a result update on Birla Corporation. Sales from the newly commissioned Kundanganj and Mukutban facilities grew 20% and 8% YoY respectively in Q2FY27, with Mukutban dispatching ~6.5 lakh tons during the quarter.

detailedSummary.heading: Investment thesis
bullets: Sales from the newly commissioned Kundanganj and Mukutban facilities grew 20% and 8% YoY respectively in Q2FY27, with Mukutban dispatching ~6.5 lakh tons during the quarter.
Sales from the newly commissioned Kundanganj and Mukutban facilities grew 20% and 8% YoY respectively in Q2FY27, with Mukutban dispatching ~6.5 lakh tons during the quarter.

detailedSummary.heading: Financial performance
bullets: Management maintained its earlier timelines for the ~6.2 mt of capacity additions by FY29 (taking capacity to ~27.6 mt), with no delays flagged. • Volume – Consolidated cement sales volume rose 6.9% YoY to 4.54mt in Q2FY27 from 4.25mt in Q2FY26, with capacity utilization steady at 85% despite excessive rainfall disrupting construction activity in core markets.

Management refrained from giving a specific H2 volume forecast, citing multiple variables: drought in parts of Maharashtra and Rajasthan, a likely demand slowdown in Uttar Pradesh once the election model code of conduct applies, and receding floods in North Bihar and Eastern UP.
Non-trade prices, which had plummeted, corrected towards the end of the quarter, but this does little for BCL given its heavy skew to trade and blended cement.

detailedSummary.heading: Risks and concerns
bullets: Expansion projects (~6.2 mt by FY29), renewable power, mine development and efficiency initiatives remain the key spending areas, and the timeline guidance for upcoming capacities has been maintained. • Incentive – BCL accrued ~₹30crs of state incentives in Q2FY27 (₹63crs in H1FY27), mainly for Mukutban and Kundanganj, with a closing receivable balance of ~₹545crs; no incentives were received during the quarter.

While medium-term positives include the Kundanganj and Mukutban ramp-ups, capacity expansion to ~27.6mt by FY29, and expected fuel cost relief from captive coal and renewables starting H2FY27, near-term earnings remain constrained and expansion risks further leverage given net debt of ₹2,432crs and a weak debt service coverage ratio of 0.93x.

detailedSummary.heading: Key takeaways
bullets: Non-trade prices, which had plummeted, corrected towards the end of the quarter, but this does little for BCL given its heavy skew to trade and blended cement.

detailedSummary.heading: Financial performance
bullets: Sterile Injectables grew on tech transfer revenue from the new Line 3 at Spokane, now working with 13+ products across 5+ customers while generics grew on new launches and share gains in existing products.

detailedSummary.heading: Valuation
bullets: Broker rating: BUY.

blurb: While Revenue and EBITDA grew by 22% and 6% respectively, PAT remained flat.
execSummary: IDBI Capital published a result update on Clean Science and Technology. Target ₹750 (+12% vs ₹668). While Revenue and EBITDA grew by 22% and 6% respectively, PAT remained flat.

detailedSummary.heading: Investment thesis
bullets: While Revenue and EBITDA grew by 22% and 6% respectively, PAT remained flat.
While Revenue and EBITDA grew by 22% and 6% respectively, PAT remained flat.

detailedSummary.heading: Financial performance
bullets: Consolidated Revenue growth was majorly led by growth in realisations and improved HALS volumes on YoY basis.  Pressure on Gross margins: Gross margins declined sharply by 360 bps QoQ to 57.3% owing the sharp rise in raw material prices brought about by the Middle East Crisis.

Sharp rise in coal and freight costs further exacerbated margin pressures.  Market Share Retention Strategy: Phenol prices in China were around 16% lower than Indian prices which gave Chinese producers a cost advantage to source at a lower cost.

Although demand remained resilient, pass through of costs to customers was difficult leading to margin compression on sequential basis  HALS: HALS Revenue doubled in Q2FY27 on YoY basis on the back of robust HALS volume growth.

detailedSummary.heading: Valuation
bullets: Target price ₹750 against a market price of ₹668 at the report date.

CFCL has completed trials of advanced grades of HALS and commercial launch is expected in H2FY27  Valuation: We revise our rating to HOLD on the stock with revised TP of Rs 750 at 30xFY28 expected earnings in light of the macro induced margin pressures along with growth moderation in principal products.
Utilization is ~30%–40%, targeted at 55%–60% in coming quarters.  Backward Integration: An epoxidation facility is already running.

HALS capacity of ~11,500 tons is planned to reach ~12,500 tons through advanced grades.  Product Launches: Performance Chemical 2 (ATBS) is expected to start commercial production in Jan–Feb (Q4FY27), targeting 20%–25% utilization in year one.

detailedSummary.heading: Risks and concerns
bullets: Strong volume recovery for principal products and better ramp up for HALS will be key monitorables.
Management won’t be first to raise prices and risk losing market share.  HALS Ramp-Up: HALS revenue doubled YoY and was ~22% of sales (~Rs660Mn).

detailedSummary.heading: Key takeaways
bullets: Although demand remained resilient, pass through of costs to customers was difficult leading to margin compression on sequential basis  HALS: HALS Revenue doubled in Q2FY27 on YoY basis on the back of robust HALS volume growth.

bullets: Strong India momentum and pipeline opportunities are offset by limited near-term US earnings visibility and margin recovery.

detailedSummary.heading: Financial performance
bullets: Business performance: Lupin’s revenue grew 11.1% YoY to Rs78.3bn, led by India (+14.7% to Rs23.8bn), other developed markets (+45.7% to Rs11.8bn; Europe, Australia, and Canada, with Europe delivering double-digit growth even ex-VISUfarma), and API (+20.2% to Rs3.1bn).

US revenue grew 9.3% to Rs30.2bn, but was nearly flat in dollar terms at US$317mn (+0.2%), as higher base volumes and seasonal demand were offset by tolvaptan pricing pressure following two additional generic entrants.
EBITDA fell 8.4% to Rs19.6bn, with margins contracting by 532bps to 25.0%, owing to US price erosion, higher employee and field costs, settlement-linked licence fees, and increased R&D.

detailedSummary.heading: Valuation
bullets: Broker rating: HOLD.
Valuation: We maintain our HOLD rating with a revised target price of Rs2,144 (earlier: Rs2,669), derived by rolling forward our valuation to Sep-28E and applying 25x FY28E EPS.

The lower target price reflects the moderation in our earnings estimates, with FY28 expected to be a transition year as intensifying competition and erosion in key US products weigh on profitability, while elevated R&D and commercialisation investments constrain operating leverage.
Launch is planned for Q1FY28, targeting select channels rather than a direct-to-consumer play.

detailedSummary.heading: Risks and concerns
bullets: Outlook: We estimate revenue of Rs306.2bn, Rs313.3bn, and Rs336.3bn in FY27E, FY28E, and FY29E, respectively.
India will remain the key growth driver, supported by the management's guidance of 1.2-1.3x IPM growth and increasing chronic contribution.

bullets: EBITDA fell 8.4% to Rs19.6bn, with margins contracting by 532bps to 25.0%, owing to US price erosion, higher employee and field costs, settlement-linked licence fees, and increased R&D.

detailedSummary.heading: Financial performance
bullets: Gross margin contracted by 758bps YoY to 42.5% on raw material and freight inflation and a higher India mix, limiting EBITDA growth to 12.7% YoY at Rs5.9bn (margin 17.0%, -542bps YoY), in line with estimates.

Adjusted PAT rose 6.6% YoY to Rs2.83bn but missed NBIE and consensus by 10.8% and 8.5%, respectively, on higher interest and depreciation.  Outlook: Management expects raw material and freight inflation to persist over the next few quarters.

Price hikes of 2-3% (mainly in India) did not fully offset cost inflation in 2QFY27, and higher freight (~6.5% of sales) is yet to be passed through, with export pricing to remain tactical between volume and profitability.
